findings.description: The open-mount refusal is keyed on the suite arm's `eval_only` flag combined with the environment variable LOA_ABLATION_BATCH_CONTEXT=1. Both inputs are fully under the control of whoever invokes pipeline-run.sh: the suite file is a CLI argument (--suite-file) and the variable is set per-invocation (the header even documents doing so by hand). The gate does not look at the thing it is meant to protect, the `oracle_open: true` toggle. A suite file that sets `oracle_open: true` and omits `eval_only` passes straight through, because validate-suite.sh (which enforces that pairing) is not run by pipeline-run.sh. Nothing in the run directory records that the trial was launched outside a batch, so a manually launched open-mount trial is indistinguishable from a batch one downstream.
findings.failure_mode: An operator or script runs the open-mount (answer-visible) review arm outside run-ablation.sh, either by exporting the variable or by editing the suite to drop `eval_only`. The resulting rows carry oracle leakage yet look like ordinary trials, and the only downstream exclusion (ablation-report.py) keys on the same editable suite flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse on the capability, not the label: `[[ "$(jq -r '.toggles.oracle_open' <<<"$ARM_DEF")" == true ]]` should also require the batch context (and `eval_only: true`), independent of validate-suite. Record `eval_only` and `batch_context` into meta/arm-evidence.txt so took-effect.sh and the report can verify provenance per run rather than trusting the suite file.

findings.cross_file_justification: pipeline-run.sh records `oracle_open` and `mount_overlay=none` in meta/arm-evidence.txt per run (shown by the new bats assertions), but ablation-report.py's component selection consults only the suite file's `eval_only` flag, so the per-run evidence that would catch a mislabelled open-mount arm is never used in the exclusion decision.
findings.description: `components` drops an arm from the shipped-default decision set solely when the suite arm declares `eval_only: true`. The report never cross-checks the rows' recorded evidence (`oracle_open`, `mount_overlay`) against that flag. A suite revision that renames or relabels the open-mount arm without `eval_only`, or rows generated under a differently-flagged suite, would be counted as a decision component with oracle-leaked results.
findings.failure_mode: Open-mount (answer-visible) review-catch rows inflate a decision component's effect estimate, producing a false 'H1 established' or component-retained decision.
findings.suggested_fix: When building `components`, also exclude (or fail hard on) any arm whose rows carry arm-evidence `oracle_open=true` or `mount_overlay=none` on a review-catch task, and emit a provenance line when the suite flag and the recorded evidence disagree.
